applies_why: The judge text uses the word not by itself establishing begetting as a reason to decide UNDERDETERMINED in D4.
quote: D4 vs C3 (Luke 2:48): UNDERDETERMINED -- C3’s “thy father” is a plain register, but [CR3] answers that the narrator avoids “father” and the word does not by itself establish begetting; read together the fact of begetting remains open -- GROUND: C3 narrows away the claim that the word names a begetter, so it does not contradict D4’s supposition point.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: “That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED”: (1) it forbids treating one verse’s failure to establish or contradict a link as a reason for UNDERDETERMINED; (2) it applies only where the judge expressly says a single verse is being used, not where the judge says a word/verse does not by itself establish the point.
why: Because D4’s UNDERDETERMINED rests on the word not by itself establishing begetting and the fact remaining open, the judge uses a single verse’s insufficiency as a ground for UNDERDETERMINED, which K-S2 forbids.
